title: Your first program: print and read
instructions:
## The edit-run-check loop

Every program you will ever write goes round the same loop: **edit** the text, **run** it, read what happened, fix it, run again. This lab gets you round the loop a few times.

The editor already prints a welcome line. Press **Run** and look at the black output box.

## Do this

1. Below the welcome line, read a name from the user with `input()` and keep it in a variable called `name`.
2. Print `Hello, Ama!` (with the name the user typed, a comma, and an exclamation mark).
3. Read a second line, the user's town, into a variable `town`, and print `Greetings from Ho.` (with a full stop).

The program input box under the editor holds what `input()` will read: one line per call. Change it and run again to see your program greet someone else.

## Why it matters

`print` and `input` are the whole of a program's conversation with a person. Everything else is deciding what to say.
